transcript:
Meeting: Data residency discovery - Ironclad Bank
Date/Time: 2026-03-06 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Redwood SE), Tom Whitman (Ironclad Head of Cloud), Priya Rao (CISO), Samir Patel (Lead ML Eng), Jillian (Legal)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for taking the time, really appreciate it. quick agenda - understand your residency/compliance constraints, current stack, and discuss hosted vs dedicated vs private options.

[00:22] Tom Whitman: yeah thanks maya. quick background: we run a mixed cloud estate, primary regions are us-east-1 and eu-west-1. We have a bunch of customer PII and transaction data that sits in the EU for EU customers and obviously US for US customers. we're evaluating LLMs for internal assistants and a few customer-facing features. major question: can we keep EU data in-region and meet our audit retention requirements?

[00:45] Maya Chen: totally. that's one of the common asks. Diego, do you want to add how Redwood handles residency across hosted/dedicated/private?

[00:52] Diego Ruiz: sure. short answer: Hosted can be region-restricted - we have datacenters and region pins, but for strongest compliance we recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated is reserved capacity in our cloud with per-customer isolation and region pinning; Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane, VPC peering, and an on-prem option if you need air gap. note: hosted logs may be retained for support/debug by default but we can adjust retention and redaction policies for enterprise contracts.

[01:18] Priya Rao: when you say "retain logs for support" - what kinds of logs, where are they stored, and can we stop any customer PII from being logged at all?

[01:30] Diego Ruiz: good question. we separate request metadata (timestamps, route, model id, latency) from full request/response content. for Hosted the request payload may be stored short-term for troubleshooting; for Dedicated and Private we can provide options to disable request/response retention, enable strict PII redaction, or route logs into your SIEM via syslog/CloudWatch. we also support customer-managed KMS for encrypting any persisted artifacts.

[02:05] Samir Patel: Do you have HIPAA experience? some of our teams touch small sets of PHI in edge cases. Also need to know if the embeddings store or cache could leak PHI even transiently.

[02:18] Lena Park: we've onboarded healthcare customers; we offer HIPAA BAA for Dedicated and Private setups. embeddings and KV cache can be configured to not persist across sessions - ephemeral cache only - and for strict setups the cache can be disabled. we do need to confirm model behavior too - inference outputs should be audited as well.

[02:45] Tom Whitman: okay. on GDPR specifically, we need to ensure EU customer data never leaves eu-west-1. that includes logs, backups, and any model variant that might route to another region for fallback. is that possible?

[03:05] Diego Ruiz: yes, with Dedicated we can pin workloads to region and configure smart routing policies to avoid cross-region fallback. Private on-prem or VPC gives you full control. for Hosted, we can do region isolation but there are caveats around cross-region fallbacks during outages - we can include contractual obligations and runbook for that.

[03:27] Jillian (Legal): timeline question - procurement will need SOC2, ISO27001 certs, pen test summary, and contract language about data residency. Do you have a standard security packet we can review?

[03:40] Maya Chen: yes, we'll send our security packet and SOC2/ISO docs. Diego will include a high-level network diagram and options for KMS integration.

[03:52] Priya Rao: KMS/HSM - we need to own keys for some regulated flows. do you support customer-managed keys and HSM-backed keys?

[04:03] Diego Ruiz: yes - Dedicated and Private support bring-your-own-KMS; HSM integrations are available for Private (on-prem HSM or cloud HSM like AWS CloudHSM). For Hosted, we offer customer-managed KMS for encrypting customer artifacts but not for model weights - weights are managed separately.

[04:28] Samir Patel: about models themselves - if we use an open model in Redwood Hosted that you maintain, is there any possibility of telemetry or model updates pulling data outside region?

[04:40] Lena Park: model updates are versioned. for Dedicated we can pin to a particular model version and disable auto-updates. Hosted may auto-roll minor updates for security patches but we can control that for enterprise agreements. telemetry is aggregated; we can opt out of telemetry for enterprise tenants.

[05:05] Tom Whitman: retention - we have a minimum log retention for audit: 7 years for some financial records. Are you able to store and serve logs for that long, and can they be exported to our long-term archive?

[05:20] Diego Ruiz: we can support long retention via Dedicated/Private and export hooks to your S3/GCS archives. Hosted has default retention windows but enterprise add-ons allow extended retention and export. need to confirm legal hold processes as well.

[05:42] Priya Rao: another point - redaction and masking. we need ability to automatically mask account numbers and tokens at ingestion, ideally with a pre-ingest sanitizer. does Redwood provide that or do we need to layer it?

[05:58] Lena Park: we have pre-ingest pipelines that can run regex-based redaction and a small transform layer. for advanced use we often recommend running pre-processing on your side in your VPC before sending to Redwood, especially for the most sensitive PII.

[06:20] Samir Patel: performance tradeoffs - Dedicated vs Private. we want sub-200ms 95th percentile for short prompts at 50 qps. how realistic is that?

[06:33] Diego Ruiz: with Dedicated and tuned batching/quantization we can hit that for certain model sizes; Private on-prem can also meet it but depends on hardware. we'll need to size GPUs (A100s or L40s) and look at sequence lengths. I can rough out a sizing estimate.

[06:52] Tom Whitman: procurement will push back on cost vs risk. If we go Hosted with contractual residency guarantees, is there any SLA for cross-region failover?

[07:04] Maya Chen: Hosted SLAs cover availability but cross-region failover is an operational risk. For ironclad-grade guarantees we tend to recommend Dedicated with capacity commitments or Private for full control. We can include fallback playbooks in the contract.

[07:20] Jillian (Legal): can we get sample contract clauses for data residency and data deletion on contract termination?

[07:28] Maya Chen: yes we'll include sample language.

[07:32] Priya Rao: audit logs - we need tamper-evident audit logs for a number of services. Do you provide append-only audit logs or do we need to ship to our SIEM?

[07:44] Diego Ruiz: we surface audit logs and can stream them to customer-managed destinations. For stronger tamper-evident requirements we recommend storing them in your own immutable storage or cloud WORM buckets; Private deployments can be configured to write directly into those systems.

[08:05] Samir Patel: any limitations around exporting embeddings or vector stores? we need to ensure that vectors generated for EU users are stored in-region and can be deleted on request.

[08:18] Lena Park: embeddings storage can be region-scoped. We also provide delete APIs for user-level and dataset-level deletion requests - we can demonstrate that in the SE deep dive.

[08:33] Tom Whitman: are there any customers in fintech who have done Dedicated or Private with similar requirements? references would help procurement.

[08:45] Maya Chen: yes, we have several regional banks and fintechs. we'll share anonymized references and a case study about a Dedicated deployment with strict residency controls.

[09:00] Jillian (Legal): how about data subject access requests (DSARs) - if a EU user requests deletion, what is the process?

[09:10] Diego Ruiz: we support deletion endpoints and will coordinate to remove derivatives like embeddings if needed. for Hosted we need to confirm retention windows; Dedicated/Private give you more immediate control.

[09:26] Samir Patel: one more technical: do you ever log raw prompt+response in traces that could be copied to third-party APMs? We try to avoid third-party leakage of sensitive content.

[09:37] Lena Park: tracing hooks can be configured to exclude payloads; we can send only metadata to APMs or route traces to your own APM instance in your VPC.

[09:50] Tom Whitman: okay good. Let's talk timeline - we want to run a 6-week pilot, ideally starting late March. Pilot goal: validate EU residency, log redaction, and performance at 50 qps. Is that feasible?

[10:04] Diego Ruiz: feasible. we'd recommend Dedicated pilot w/ region pinning or Private pilot if you want full control. For Dedicated we can provision reserved nodes for the pilot; I'll produce a sizing + cost estimate.

[10:20] Priya Rao: procurement and security will need a workshop with your security engineering to go through the questionnaire. can we target next week for that?

[10:30] Maya Chen: yes - I'll send availability. Diego, can you be on the workshop?

[10:36] Diego Ruiz: yep happy to.

[10:38] Jillian (Legal): one final ask: sample data deletion SLA and proof of deletion procedures.

[10:45] Maya Chen: we'll include proof-of-deletion steps and an option for data escrow on contract termination if needed.

[10:52] Tom Whitman: cool. I think that covers most of it. quick recap?

[10:58] Maya Chen: recap: 1) Redwood to send security packet (SOC2, ISO, pen test) and network diagram; 2) Redwood SE to size Dedicated pilot for 50 qps and provide cost estimate; 3) schedule SE-led technical workshop next week for security questionnaire & DSAR process; 4) Ironclad to share their resident policy and list of workloads for pilot. action owners and due dates in the notes.

[11:25] Tom Whitman: thanks all. look forward to docs.

[11:30] Priya Rao: thanks.

[11:32] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the docs and proposed times.

[11:40] [call ended]

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings ("redaction" transcribed as "reduction" in places) and speaker labels are manually corrected where possible. Shared artifacts: security_packet_link.pdf (sent), dedicated-pilot-sizing.xlsx (to follow), sample-contract-clauses.docx (to follow).
